fields.explanation: const fixes the binding obj (writing obj = {} again would throw), but the object it refers to stays mutable, so obj.x = 1 adds a property and obj.x reads 1. A TypeError occurs only when reassigning obj itself, or, in strict mode, when writing to an object frozen with Object.freeze. undefined would mean the assignment was silently ignored, which does not happen to an ordinary, unfrozen object.

fields.explanation: When a function is called as obj.get(), the object before the dot becomes this for that call, so this.n reads obj.n, which is 5. For this.n to be undefined, this would have to be something other than obj, which happens only when the method is detached (const g = obj.get; g()) or written as an arrow function; neither applies here. There is no TypeError because this is a valid object.

fields.explanation: Arrow functions do not get their own this; they use the this of the scope in which they are written. That scope is the top level of the script, not obj, and in a classic browser script top-level this is the global object (window), which has no n, so the result is undefined. In an ES module top-level this is undefined and the same code throws a TypeError, which is why the script type matters. To read obj.n, write get() { return this.n; } instead.

problems: explanation claims top-level this in a Node CommonJS file is the global object; it is module.exports (the call still yields undefined, but the stated reason is false)

fields.explanation: JSON has no representation for undefined, so JSON.stringify omits any object property whose value is undefined, leaving the string "{}". It does not write undefined, and it does not substitute null for object properties — although inside an array an undefined element does become null. Functions and symbols are dropped the same way, which is why data can silently go missing when it is serialized.

problems: "serialised" is British spelling; the question bank and shared code use "serialize"

notes: Every runtime claim verified; only the spelling needed changing.
